newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco floats 20 pct of silver mine on bourse.
newsitem.headline: Morocco floats 20 pct of silver mine on bourse.

text.p: Morocco floated 20 percent of its minority stake in the Imiter silver mine worth $13.7 million, a bourse official said on Monday.
"The flotation of 20 state stake in Imiter firm worth 130.3 million dirhams ($13.7 million), or 396 dirhams per share, was floated on Monday," the official said.
Subscription will be closed on June 13, he added.
It is the 12th floatation of the bourse since the government launched its privatisation programme in 1993, a broker said.
The authorities plan to sell stakes in 113 firms, including banks and sugar plants by end 1998.

The state holds a stake of 33 percent of Societe Metallurgique d'Imiter (SMI) through the state-run Bureau des Recherches et Participations Minieres (BRPM), the remaining 67 percent of the capital is held by Morocco's largest private conglomerate ONA group.
Last year, ONA purchased four mines, including stakes in Imiter for more than 400 million dirhams.

One of the 10 most profitable silver mines in the world with an estimated 1,000 grammes of silver per tonne of ore, Imiter has a productive life of up to eight years, Upline Securities stockbroker said.
The mine is located in the province of Ouarzazate, 500 kms south east of the Moroccan capital of Rabat.
Imiter, which has a capital of 164.5 million dirhams, posted a turnover of 258.1 million dirhams in 1996, down from 309.8 million in 1995.
Imiter is expected to be listed on the bourse on June 17, 1997, the ministry added.
